llm.summary: This skill is not clearly malicious, but it exposes broader paid, persistent, and account-mutating ARI capabilities than its narrow seller action-plan description suggests.

dimensions.detail: Network access is constrained to the official ARI HTTPS origin, but the skill still needs a bearer API key, account/profile access, billing checks, local export writes, and broad ARI account actions that exceed the advertised specialized action-plan scope.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is a local skill package using a Python standard-library CLI; setup uses browser authorization and stores an ARI API key locally rather than installing dependencies or fetching executable updates.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions disclose many safeguards, but they also direct agents to accept service-side auto-confirmed paid runs and the specialized operations command exposes --workflow and --focus overrides despite documentation saying this package is fixed to audit/action.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists credentials in ~/.ari/config.json and can change durable ARI account state, including autoconfirm thresholds, collection schedules, competitor bindings, watch state, alert read state, and workbench review status.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The manifest frames the skill as a single-ASIN seller action-plan tool, while the included instructions and CLI cover VOC reports, keyword/ad-adjacent analysis, exports, monitoring, competitor management, alerts, leaderboard queries, workbench status changes, and paid advice generation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable granting this skill access to your ARI account and review data, and review the auto-confirm, monitoring, competitor, export, and workflow settings before use. For least surprise, set paid actions to ask every time and avoid using this package for ad keyword decisions or broader account operations unless you intend those actions.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Confirmed in substance: SKILL.md and ari.py expose a broad ARI operations surface beyond the narrow single-ASIN action-plan framing.
[AE1] unexpected: Downgraded: scripts/ari.py is present in the workspace and was inspected; this is not evidence of analysis evasion in the submitted artifact.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Confirmed in part: the skill says it is not for advertising decisions, but it includes a keywords workflow that produces PPC/search-term and negative-keyword outputs.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Confirmed: schedule, competitors, watch, autoconfirm, and workbench commands can make persistent account changes outside a one-off action-plan workflow, though several are documented with user-consent language.
[LP3] unexpected: Partially supported: the implementation has strong official-domain checks, but there is no manifest-level least-privilege boundary limiting this specialized package to only audit/action operations.
[SQP-1] expected: Broad natural-language triggering is expected for a user-facing analysis skill, but it increases the risk that general review-analysis requests route into paid or state-changing workflows.
[SQP-2] expected: Local API-key storage is expected for this integration and is disclosed; the code writes with 0600 permissions, but users should still treat the machine as trusted.
[EA2] unexpected: Confirmed as a material concern: VOC/analyze may execute and consume credits when the backend returns autoConfirm, and the skill tells the agent not to ask again afterward.
[T05] unexpected: Confirmed: operation_payload prefers caller-supplied --workflow and --focus over skill-defaults.json, so the specialized audit/action boundary can be bypassed if the ARI server/account supports other combinations.
